lessons.subject: English
lessons.title: Prefixes
lessons.summary: Add letters to the start of a word to change what it means.
lessons.curriculum: Year 3 and 4 English, spelling: prefixes such as un-, dis-, mis- and re-, and how they change meaning
pages: A prefix is a group of letters you add to the start of a word. It changes the word's meaning.
The prefixes ‘un’ and ‘dis’ often mean ‘not’. Unhappy means not happy. Dislike means not like.
The prefix ‘re’ means ‘again’, so rebuild means build again. The prefix ‘mis’ means ‘wrongly’, so misspell means spell wrongly.

check.question: What does ‘unkind’ mean?
check.explanation: The prefix ‘un’ means ‘not’, so unkind means not kind.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Roman numerals on a clock
lessons.summary: Read Roman numerals from I to XII, as on some clocks.
lessons.curriculum: Year 3 maths: tell and write the time from an analogue clock, including using Roman numerals from I to XII
pages: The Romans used letters to write numbers. I means 1, V means 5 and X means 10.
Put I after a letter to add 1. So VI is 6 and XI is 11.
Put I before a letter to take away 1. So IV is 4 and IX is 9.
Some clocks use Roman numerals. XII is at the top, for 12 o'clock.

check.question: What number is IX?
check.explanation: I before X means 1 less than 10, so IX is 9.

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.title: Magnets
lessons.summary: Find out how magnets attract and repel.
lessons.curriculum: Year 3 science: describe magnets as having 2 poles, predict whether 2 magnets will attract or repel, and identify some magnetic materials
pages: A magnet pulls some metals towards it. We say the magnet attracts them.
Iron and steel are magnetic. Some metals, like copper and aluminium, are not. Wood, plastic and paper are not magnetic.
Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole. Opposite poles attract. The same poles push each other away, or repel.

check.question: Which of these will a magnet attract?
check.explanation: Iron is magnetic, so a magnet attracts an iron nail.

lessons.subject: History
lessons.title: Stone Age Britain
lessons.summary: Find out how people in Britain lived in the Stone Age.
lessons.curriculum: Key stage 2 history: changes in Britain from the Stone Age to the Iron Age
pages: The Stone Age is named after the tools people made from stone. They often used a hard stone called flint.
At first, people hunted animals and gathered plants to eat. They moved from place to place to find food.
Later, people started to farm. They could stay in one place and build villages.
You can still visit Skara Brae in Orkney, Scotland. It is a Stone Age village about 5,000 years old.

check.question: Why is it called the Stone Age?
check.explanation: People made many of their tools from stone, such as flint.
